subject: Qualification: Deployment mode & PoC plan for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment Mode Discussion / Next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Run a Proof-of-Concept to validate latency, throughput, and security for your customer-facing search/chat use case (English + Spanish).
- Key constraints: data residency (US-only), strict KMS controls for keys, and SSO/SCIM integration for internal users.
- Primary stakeholders on your side: you (Product lead), Priya (Security), Arjun (Platform/Infra).

Deployment mode options discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest to ship) — Redwood-managed, lowest operational overhead but does not meet your data residency / KMS isolation requirements today.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in our hosting; can provide isolation and better unit economics, supports customer-managed keys in most regions.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation, VPC peering or on-prem installer, supports customer KMS/HSM and audit log retention controls (best fit for regulated data).

Our read on fit: based on Priya’s notes about KMS and data residency, Private (VPC/on-prem) looks like the likely path for production. For the PoC we can run a short Private-VPC trial or a hybrid approach (Dedicated with strong KMS controls) if you want to accelerate delivery.

Proposed PoC plan (high level):
- Duration: 4–6 weeks (6 weeks if we do Private on-prem evaluation)
- Success criteria (examples):
  * Latency: p95 < 120ms for typical query sizes
  * Throughput: sustained 50 qps with retries under 5%
  * Integration: SSO + SCIM, KMS integration validated, audit logs accessible
  * Qualitative: generated results meet product team quality bar on 200 evaluation prompts
- Deliverables: architecture diagram, PoC deployment (VPC or Dedicated), integration checklist, short report with metrics and recommended next steps

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Confirm target deployment mode for PoC (Private-VPC vs Dedicated).
2) Confirm stakeholders and an availability window for kickoff (we can start as early as 23 Mar if approvals are in place).
3) Security request: Priya — can you confirm what evidence you need up front (SOC2, pen test, architecture diagram)? We’ve attached our SOC2 and a draft PoC plan for reference.

Attachments: PoC-Plan-Acme-Private-VPC.pdf (draft), SOC2-Redwood.pdf, SOW-PoC-Acme.docx (draft)

I’ll loop Marissa (solutions) on the technical kickoff once you confirm mode and timing. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min sync to finalize the plan later this week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-corp.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment Mode Discussion / Next steps

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

- At a high level we are leaning toward Private VPC/on-prem because of the KMS and data residency requirements.
- Timeline: we need to get security sign-off before any on-prem work. If we do Private, expect a slightly longer lead time (network approvals, firewall rules, etc.). Can you confirm typical lead time for Private PoCs?
- Priya — can you outline the docs you need? We need SOC2 and an architecture diagram at minimum.

Assuming Private, please send a proposed kickoff week and a short list of prerequisites so we can internal approvals.

Sam
Product Lead, Acme Corp
sam.lee@acme-corp.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-corp.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment Mode Discussion / Next steps

Sam — thanks, confirming Private VPC is a common path and we can support a PoC with that setup. A few specifics and an updated PoC plan attached.

Private PoC typical lead time:
- Prep & approvals: 1–2 weeks (network whitelists, KMS provisioning, NDA if required)
- Deployment & integration: 1–3 weeks depending on access and infra (on-prem will be longer than VPC peering)
- Validation & reporting: 1 week

So total: ~3–6 weeks depending on the shape of the environment. For your case I’d budget 6 weeks to be conservative.

Proposed PoC (Private-VPC) — checklist/high level:
- Week 0: Kickoff + network connectivity planning (contacts + firewall rules)
- Week 1: Provisioning (VPC peering / private link) + KMS integration (customer-managed keys)
- Week 2–4: Deploy model, run integration tests, run load tests, collect metrics
- Week 5: QA and product team evaluation on the 200 prompt set; iterate on prompts/configs
- Week 6: Final report, recommendations, and pathway to production (Dedicated or Private full deployment)

Success criteria (concrete):
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms for target prompt distribution
- Throughput: sustained 50 qps with auto-scaling behavior within defined SLAs
- Security: KMS integration verified, audit logs accessible for 90-day retention as required
- Ops: token-level cost estimate and per-route cost analysis delivered

Attachments in this thread: PoC-Plan-Acme-Private-VPC.pdf, SOC2-Redwood.pdf, SOW-PoC-Acme.docx (all draft).

Marissa (cc) — would you be available for a 30-min technical kickoff next week? Please propose 2 time slots and we’ll align with Sam/Priya.

Ben

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment Mode Discussion / Next steps

Thanks — we will review the SOC2 and the PoC plan. A few initial asks from Security: 

1) Please provide an architecture diagram showing control plane vs data plane, and where KMS calls originate.
2) Details on network requirements (ports, IP ranges, egress rules) so our infra team can pre-approve firewall changes.
3) KMS/HSM compatibility matrix and whether Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs.

We can set a kickoff for next Tuesday (17 Mar) afternoon 2–3pm PT if that works — to review prerequisites and timeline. If Redwood can share the architecture diagram and a short runbook before then, Security will be in a better position to sign off quickly.

Priya Rao
Head of Security, Acme Corp
priya.rao@acme-corp.com
